nodes.description: Intravitreal bevacizumab or ranibizumab is the mainstay for the neovascular complication. A systematic review of 31 cases found good responses when treatment began immediately after symptom onset, with the delay between first symptoms and treatment determining subretinal scar formation and functional prognosis; 11 of 20 eyes with acuity reported before and after treatment kept driving vision, while 5 worsened. A 12-year two-sister series found a treat-and-extend schedule better than pro re nata at preventing recurrence. The therapy addresses the neovascular lesion and not the underlying dystrophy, so atrophic progression continues.

nodes.description: Disulfide-linked mutant TIMP-3 is cleared from the extracellular matrix more slowly than wild-type protein by retinal pigment epithelial cells. Transcript levels are not raised in affected eyes, so the accumulation is post-translational rather than an increase in expression. The process is bound as protein catabolism of TIMP-3, decreased, because the defect is the clearance of one protein from the matrix, not breakdown of the matrix as a whole.

nodes.description: One 35-year-old patient with aggressive bilateral macular neovascularization and p.Ser204Cys, who showed disease activity on intravitreal bevacizumab and was controlled on repeated intravitreal triamcinolone, had no signs of disease activity over 18 months of subcutaneous adalimumab. The authors propose that the TIMP3 variant raises local tumour necrosis factor alpha because TIMP-3 restrains its shedding by ADAM17. The rationale is untested for this patient's allele. The only measurement a 2024 mechanistic review reports is for a different allele, Ser179Cys (Ser156Cys in secreted-protein numbering), which inhibits ADAM17 as well as wild-type TIMP-3 does; the same review states that the other SFD mutants, Ser204Cys (Ser181Cys) among them, have not been profiled. Because the case for a TNF arm rests on one patient plus TIMP-3 biology measured outside the eye, the entry records the treatment and its single-patient evidence without a mechanism node or pathophysiology target, and holds the question open in the discussions section.

nodes.description: TIMP-3 is made by the retinal pigment epithelium and is normally a component of Bruch's membrane, where it regulates the thickness of that matrix by inhibiting matrix metalloproteinases. In SFD eyes the thickened membrane and the sub-RPE deposits label strongly for TIMP-3, and the protein is increased in the extracellular matrix of patient-derived RPE, so the mutant protein accumulates in the compartment where the wild-type protein normally works.

nodes.description: A heterozygous TIMP3 variant, in most reported cases a missense change in exon 5 affecting the C-terminal domain of the protein, adds or removes a cysteine residue and so disturbs the arrangement of the conserved cysteines and disulfide bonds that hold the tertiary structure together. A minority of reported alleles do not alter a cysteine (for example His158Arg) or lie outside exon 5 (Ser38Cys in exon 1), and one nonsense allele leaves an unpaired cysteine. Mutant protein continues to be expressed and to localize to the extracellular matrix, so the primary consequence is an altered protein rather than its absence.

nodes.description: A knock-in carrying the disease-associated Ser156Cys substitution in the orthologous murine gene. At 8 months it shows abnormalities of the inner aspect of Bruch's membrane and of the adjacent RPE basal microvilli, with increased Timp3 in Bruch's membrane, while retinal function recorded electrodiagnostically stays normal for life. Comparable changes appear in normal littermates only at 30 months. The same allele shows reduced MMP inhibition with raised MMP2 and bFGF and accentuated laser induced choroidal neovascular leakage, more membrane-associated VEGFR-2 in endothelium, and RPE and photoreceptor degeneration at sodium iodate doses that spare wild-type mice.
